title: Ash-Sharh 94:1-3 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: Ash-Sharh, Ad-Duha 1 to 8 and applying the rules
source: Written for quran/y3 lesson 30 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Ash-Sharh 94:1-3 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 30. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ (١) وَوَضَعْنَا عَنكَ وِزْرَكَ (٢) ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ (٣)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Did We not expand for you, [O Muhammad], your breast?
And We removed from you your burden
Which had weighed upon your back

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Izhar shafawi: meem sakinah before ن
Say the meem clearly, lips closed once
Light hum, tongue ready for ك
Light hum, then a heavy ق

keywords.def: the chest; where we feel things
hiding the noon with a light hum before certain letters

questions.q: Chunk and link Ash-Sharh 94:1-3 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 94:1-3 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 94:1-3 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Find the meem sakinah in 94:1 and say its rule.
questions.a: «أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ»: izhar shafawi, the meem is clear.

questions.q: What did Allah remove from the Prophet ﷺ in 94:2 to 3?
questions.a: A heavy burden that weighed on his back.

questions.q: In «عَنكَ», the noon sakinah before ك is read with ...
questions.a: A) ikhfa'. ك is one of the 15 ikhfa' letters: the noon is hidden with a light hum.

questions.q: Ash-Sharh 94:1: «أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: When you feel worried or sad, what makes your heart feel open and light again?
questions.a: Remembering Allah, du'a and people who care; Allah opened the Prophet's ﷺ heart (94:1).
